raw_segments.text: He moved to one side to make way for the priest and server who were coming up the stairs.
They had come for the Requiem service.
By S. Vidrigae love's orders, it was sung twice a day punctually.
S. Vidrigae love went his way.
Raskolnikov stood still a moment, thought, and followed the priest into Sonya's room.
They began quietly, slowly and mournfully singing the service.
From his childhood, the thought of death and the presence of death had something oppressive
and mysteriously awful, and it was long since he had heard the Requiem service.
And there was something else here as well, too awful and disturbing.
They were all kneeling by the coffin.
Behind them, Sonya prayed, softly and, as it were, timidly weeping.
